title: Elekeiroz T-2103 butyraldehyde tower: recover the intended 20% capacity increase
source: Summers, Monaco and Britto, AIChE Spring Meeting paper 112b (2013), Sulzer/Elekeiroz; only the original tower and pre-solution operating evidence are exposed
question: T-2103 is limited near 9.5 t/h, while the project premise is 11.5 t/h. Build the existing tower, explain why added boil-up does not create useful capacity, and propose a design that reaches the premise without losing isomer separation.
data_note: Real operating history and tower geometry. The paper does not publish a feed assay, so any binary i-/n-butyraldehyde composition used in DWSIM is an explicit modelling assumption. Later hardware and operating actions, plus the 2011-2012 performance data, are withheld in outcome.json.
suggested_questions: What mechanism explains the weak response to more steam?
Can the existing shell reach 11.5 t/h?
Which field checks distinguish hydraulic flood from phase-induced foaming?
